learning_outcomes.text: Acquire knowledge for the execution, documentation, and follow-up of a Project.
Ability to carry out projects within their scope of competence and according to regulated professional attributions.
Ability to direct activities that are the object of the engineering projects described in the previous section.
Knowledge of the legal and administrative framework of a Project.
Knowledge for performing measurements, calculations, valuations, appraisals, expert reports, studies, reports, work plans and other similar tasks.
Ability to manage specifications, regulations, and mandatory standards.
Ability to organize and plan within the company, and other institutions and organizations.
Understanding and interpretation of texts and data, development of skills for their concretization and their clear and concise exposition.
Aptitude for the distribution of resources and time and their implementation in real situations.
Knowledge and capabilities to organize and manage projects. Know the organizational structure and functions of a project office.
Aptitude for drafting technical projects in works and constructions in civil buildings (that do not require architectural project) and industrial buildings.
Aptitude for drafting documents that are part of execution projects prepared in a multidisciplinary way.
Ability to analyze execution projects and their translation into the execution of works.

syllabus_topics: COMPETENCIES OF THE INDUSTRIAL TECHNICAL ENGINEER. Official College of Industrial Technical Engineers. Competencies of the Industrial Technical Engineer (Mechanical branch) and its relation to other specialties of Industrial Technical Engineering. Relationship of the Industrial Technical Engineer with other Technical Engineering fields.

REPORTS, CERTIFICATIONS, PROJECTS. Realization of Reports. Practical case. Realization of certifications. Practical case. Processing of reports and certifications. Definition of projects. Project methodology. Processing of projects in Official entities: City Council, Ministries, Supply Companies.

SPECIAL WORKS. Preliminary project. Project reform. Arbitrations. Calculation and verification of elements. Opinions and expert reports. Study of files. Valuations and appraisals. Recognitions and Inspections. Practical examples.
DESIGN PROCESSES. Introduction. Problem recognition. Problem formulation. Problem structuring. Generation and evaluation of project and design alternatives. Flow diagram. Technical Design.

RULES FOR THE INSTALLATION OF INDUSTRIES. Groups 1, II, III. Procedures for the installation of industries. General rules for certain industries. Industrial registry. Requirements an established industry must meet.
DATA COLLECTION FOR PROJECTS. Collection of Standards. Collection of Regulations.
SYMBOLOGY. Symbols for electricity, mechanics, heating, etc. Sketches of apparatus and installations. Diagrams of apparatus and installations. Diagrams. Cartograms. Organigrams. Planning.

FORMAL STRUCTURE OF THE PROJECT. Document 1. Report: content, purpose, calculation management, Standards. Doc. 2. Plans: purpose, content, sketches, diagrams, Standards. Doc. 3. Conditions: purpose, content, general conditions, material conditions, execution and economic equipment. Standards. Doc. 4. Measurements and Budget: purpose, content and structuring.
CONTRACTING FOR PROJECT EXECUTION. General conditions. Contracting process. State works contracting. Forms of awarding works.
PROJECT EXECUTION. Introduction. Types of Contracts for project execution. Execution. Certifications and Price Review.

PRINCIPLES, OBJECTIVES AND METHODS FOR PROJECT EVALUATION. Criteria and objectives of project evaluation in the Engineering process. Purpose of economic evaluation. Project evaluation process scheme. Investment and operating payments. Partial project evaluation indices. Average performance index. Recovery period. Updating and Capitalization factors. Integral methods. Net present value index. Internal rate of return. Cash generated by the project.

PROJECT PLANNING, SCHEDULING AND CONTROL. Need for programming techniques. Pert Method. Elements, Rules, Methodology. Drawing and calculation of the Pert network. Pert-times. Pert-costs. Pert-resources. Advantages and disadvantages of the Pert network. Objectives of the Pert network. Dual technique. Roy Method. Deadline-cost relationship. Evolution of costs with project progress.
GENERALITIES ON BUILDING INSTALLATIONS. Electricity and lighting. Heating and domestic hot water. Air conditioning. Ventilation and extraction. Fire prevention and protection. Other installations.

INSTALLATIONS IN PARTICULAR BUILDINGS. Factories and industrial buildings. Residential buildings. Auxiliary buildings. Service stations. Power plants and substations. Workshops. Public gathering places. Swimming pools. Schools. Hospitals. Outdoor sports fields. Other buildings.
INDUSTRIAL SAFETY. Basic concepts. Organization in the company. Safety. Generalities. Safety in installations. Occupational medicine.
SAFETY AND HEALTH PROJECT. Documentation. Plans.
ACTIVITY PROJECTS. Classified activity. Environmental impact assessment.
teaching_methods: Theoretical academic sessions (oral presentation with computer support)
Practical sessions in the classroom (exercise solving)
Autonomous practical activities (problem solving, compulsory submission of some exercises)
assessment_rules: Evaluation is based on a face-to-face theoretical and practical knowledge exam, attendance at theoretical and practical classes, and the mandatory submission of drawing sheets. Students are recommended to attend classes, study and solve drawings, submit sheets continuously, attempt proposed drawings before classroom resolution, and make use of tutorials.
